text:
Mike (Sales): Hi finance — booked an Airbnb for the team offsite last week on the company card but the host only sent a single combined charge. Need an itemized invoice to split costs across two cost centers and reimburse Sam for the extra cleaning fee he paid in cash. What do you need?
expense-bot: Reminder: Please attach receipts or invoices within 7 days of travel. Missing receipt: Airbnb *Host Reservation* - card ending 4242.
Elaine (Finance): Hi Mike — we can handle this, but we need an itemized invoice or the host's message showing the breakdown (nightly, cleaning fee, security deposit). A screenshot of the Airbnb booking page is usually fine if it shows line items and guest names. Also need proof of Sam's payment for the cleaning fee (photo of cash receipt or Venmo/Bank tx).
Mike (Sales): attaching two screenshots: 1) Airbnb confirmation page (only shows total and dates) 2) corporate card statement line: "Airbnb *HostReservation 07/12 $1,240.00". Sam paid the $75 cleaning fee in cash to the host, we don't have an official receipt, just a photo of the host's handwritten note and Sam's Venmo request thread. Is that acceptable?
Sam (Eng): I have the Venmo screenshot and a quick DM thread where the host confirms I paid cash at checkout. I can take a clearer photo of the handwritten note and the host's passport page (they gave it voluntarily) if that helps.
Jenna (People Ops): Policy refresher: per the travel policy, non-card reimbursements require either an itemized vendor receipt or a signed merchant note. Venmo screenshots are accepted only when accompanied by a vendor confirmation (email/text) and a short explanation in the expense form. Personal guest charges must be split off and covered personally (we can't reimburse personal guests).
Elaine (Finance): Got it. Mike — please do the following so we can process quickly: 1) Upload the Airbnb host message or request an itemized invoice from the host (ask for "invoice showing nightly rate, cleaning fee, taxes"). 2) Sam, upload the Venmo screenshot + the photo of the handwritten note and add a 1-2 sentence explanation in the expense form ("cleaning fee paid in cash to host on 2026-07-12 for group offsite"). 3) Mike, indicate which project codes to split the nights across (e.g., SALES-Q3 / GROWTH-Q3).
Mike (Sales): will ping the host now and request an itemized invoice, and I'll update the expense with the project split. ETA: should have host reply by EOD.
expense-bot: Expense created: "Airbnb offsite 07/12" - status: awaiting receipt. Link: https://expenses.internal/reports/EXP-2345
Elaine (Finance): If the host doesn't provide an itemized invoice, we can accept a short written attestation from the host plus the booking confirmation, but that will require a manager approval. I'll flag this for manual review.
Sam (Eng): uploaded Venmo + photo of handwritten note to the expense report (link in DM). Also added a 2-sentence note.
Mike (Sales): host replied with an email that shows nightly breakdown and cleaning fee but no tax line — attaching. Also specifying split: 60% SALES-Q3, 40% GROWTH-Q3.
Elaine (Finance): Perfect — that's sufficient. Two small items: 1) We need the host email to include their business name or GST/VAT # if applicable (not required for domestic but helpful). 2) Please change the expense category to "Lodging - Shared / Offsite" so the system applies the split correctly.
Mike (Sales): done (changed category + uploaded host email).
Elaine (Finance): OK — I'll process the reimbursements: Sam will get $75 cash reimbursement (expense will be marked as "cash reimbursement"), and the card charge will be split across the two cost centers on next billing cycle. Expect completion in 3–5 business days. :white_check_mark:
Jenna (People Ops): note for the record — remind teams to ask hosts for itemized invoices upfront for group bookings to avoid extra steps.
Mike (Sales): thanks all. sorry for the hassle. :pray:
Elaine (Finance): no problem — flagged case #FIN-2026-078 for audit trail. If anything else pops up, reply here. :mag:
